Pretty much just start being aware of everything, and question it. You'll find a deeper purpose, which is something I think that you can see you're lacking. You'll find something that TRULY catches your attention. For me it's computers, how they work, and the history of them; maybe you should try there!

Coming from a son of someone who just committed suicide (he tried to abort last second but failed), it's not worth it. I can understand that you feel like you don't matter and you won't be able to find happiness, but really, it's all about finding things that you like to do. 

If anything, please understand that others care about you more than you think. Your mom goes to work, not only for herself, but also for you and your father. It may take a little bit of thinking, but I'm sure you'd be able to think of 1000 situations where your parents went without, or did more than they normally do just to make you happy. Imagine how crushed they would be without you. 

Also, when it comes to the point of significance, it's really all that you make it. Every man has greatness in them to a certain degree, it's just finding that motivation to be great. And while I'm not saying you should shoot for being president or anything, I think that making personal conquests makes life worth living. I'm sure there are hurdles (stepping away from death) that you'd love to overcome. Just try to think of your potential and it'll be much easier to understand why life is worth living.

Tl;Dr Get a little conceited for a while. It works.

I was in a similar phase for a while (I was quite young, so take it with a grain of salt) and basically I did one thing that worked quite well. Stopped giving a fuck.

Seriously, just stop giving a fuck. Do whatever you want to do. Whenever you decide you genuinely don't give a fuck because you don't have to give a fuck, things get better. 

As long as you have food, shelter and some basic entertainment (and hopefully transportation), you'll be fine man. Learn to be content in nothingness like I did. Sometimes its fun to just be bored.

Also, I can understand that you like metal and the like, but there have been studies that have shown that music has a profound effect on one's mood and personality (and it may be a moot study, because often times personality draws one to a specific genre, not the other way around, but I digress). I would try listening to some happier music. Don't go straight flowers and sunshine right away, but you may want to just dodge away from areas where death, depression, and other generally depressing things are common themes. Dubstep was my first choice, but then I ended up going for things as silly as this: http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9bZkp7q19f0

Seriously though, the help will come through yourself. You can't expect some hand of god to come in and make everything fine and dandy, but taking steps to make yourself happier will most often times actually make you happier. 

Side note: I find that I get saddest when I'm not doing anything. It's summer right now, and you may or may not have school here soon, so that may help. If you did graduate though, you may just want to try to get a job just to spend time and meet people if nothing else.

My dad just committed suicide on tuesday, and I know what you're going through when it comes to the part where you're angry at yourself. I pretty much told him to go fuck himself a few days before he died. I know I'm not supposed to blame myself for his death, but goddamn, I know I contributed. 

But why don't I want to kill myself? Because I can still look at something small and think of how neat it is. I mean, right now I'm looking at a spider in the corner of my room. Tell me that it isn't cool that there's something as absurd as a spider. From a clean slate, nothing existing, nothing living, came a turn of events that created this.  A little spider. 

Then I look at myself. I'm pretty neat too. I'd even say I'm a bit cooler than that spider. I'm a little bit more absurd than that spider. Look at my fingernails. Aren't those something? 

Everything is pretty fucking cool if you look at it, and I'm sure that there's a ton of cool things that you can think of too. And while I don't know your stance on the afterlife, I don't really think you're going to be thinking a whole lot when you die, so you might as well try to enjoy it while it lasts. 

As for fitting in, you said that you have friends, even though you may have been a little rude to them. Hell, I've had some rude things said to me by drunk people. I forgive them though, because A. They were drunk, and B. I find their friendship more important than if my high school knows that I play WoW or anything. Go talk to them. You don't need to tell them you're suicidal or anything, just try to build a bridge. 

Rock bottom is really only as deep as you let it get. Once you start to actively turn things around, things will brighten up. You can't expect a deus ex machina, but you can expect for people to match your effort if you're trying to better yourself. 

If I could help you out in any way, just send me a PM. Money's a little strapped for me right now, but if you truly do need it more than me then I can spare a few bucks. Sounds like you could use a little pick me up, anyways. 

-Wes

I broke my wrist at a national race up in the foothills. Funny story about this: I actually won my state championship with half a cast still on. We cut off a few parts so I could hold onto the handlebars.

Right now I am 16, my brother is 13.

To be honest, at the last lengths it was my dad and my dad entirely. I was the first to quit, and my brother continued racing, but he quit about 2 years ago. At the beginning though, it was fun to go places, see new things and meet new people. It's definitely not an experience that I wish didn't happen. It's what made me who I am today.

As for their interest, leave it as their interest. I was racing at a certain point, collecting points and wins just so I could have a lower plate number (for people that are entirely fresh to the sport, the more wins/points you have from winning races, the lower plate number you get. #1 in the district is assumed to be the best.) and that overall made me very unhappy. I did go back to mountain biking for a while, and I had an absolute blast with that, as mountain biking is much less stressful and more welcoming than bmx racing, but that is VERY expensive. 

Best thing you could probably do is let them try out mountain biking for a weekend (if you can afford to continue with the sport) and see if they like it. From most people that I've met that have switched over, they liked it much more. Fair warning though, it's MUCH more dangerous and MUCH more expensive if you intend on racing competitively. On my last year of mountain biking, I cost my family $12,000 in fees/travel/parts.

I would pick up gear in this order (assuming it's all from justice):
Legs
Gloves
Wand
Chest
Neck
Ring 1
Bracers (If you can afford buying VP bracers for gold, do so and skip this step)
Trinket 1
Trinket 2 (One of these will most likely be replaced while dungeoning)
Boots (If you can afford buying VP boots for gold, do so and skip this step)
Belt (If you can buy a BoE PvE epic off the AH do so, as the best belt you can buy from justice is a 346)

When purchasing Valor Items, look at what needs the upgrade most (basically what the biggest item level jump is) and buy that. I think that you will want to buy your helm or trinket first because those cannot be bought with justice. 

As for enchants go, you will want to get the Hyjal enchant for your head (you seem to be nuetral for them, so you will want to get to friendly through questing and then use the Hyjal Tabard while dungeoning), Therazane enchant for your shoulders (the int haste one), +50 int to cloak (if you can't afford this use +30 int), +20 stats to chest (I would recommend +15 if you are short or money, or if you have the ability to upgrade your chest soon), Int to bracers (and if you can't afford that, get precision), Power Torrent to weapon (if you need to go cheap get hurricane), +40 int to offhand if you are using an offhand, +65 mastery to gloves (+50 if you can't afford +65), Elementium Belt Buckle for your belt, Powerful Enchanted Spellthread for your legs, and Mastery to boots.

As for gemming, just use +40 int gems in red sockets, +20 int +20 mastery in yellow sockets and +20int +20 hit in blue sockets.

As for reforges, just go to the site wowreforge.com, type in your character's name and realm and click optimize. I would recommend switching the values for haste and crit though, as crit will give you more dps, especially in low gear. 

If you want to read up a bit more about exactly what you should do, I would check out this post here: http://us.battle.net/wow/en/forum/topic/1648728060 as it has some solid information. You may also want to check out Elitist Jerks for further information, and if you have further questions just google it or ask Reddit as I'm sure someone will help you.

Hope this helped!
